newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds braced for volatile period.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds braced for volatile period.

text.p: *The Australian bond market is braced for a period of increased volatility amid a steady flow of data both locally and out of the U.S. this week.
*RBA holds first board meeting of the year on Tuesday.
The Australian bond market is braced for a period of increased volatility amid a steady flow of data both locally and out of the U.S. this week.
Policy making meetings are also being held in both countries over the next few days, although there is a growing feeling that they will keep their respective interest rates unchanged.

On the day the domestic bonds finished mixed as the short-end showed some realisation that a further easing in monetary policy is not a done deal, while longer dated stock benefitted from a firmer tone in U.S. Treasuries, traders said.
However, the long-end underperformed the U.S. move.

"There's been fairly light two-way trading in physicals, but notably the short-end has been squaring up ahead of the RBA meeting," one trader said. "Bills particularly seem to be unwinding as rate cut expectations are pushed out."

The Reserve Bank holds its first board meeting of the year, but economists give only a 40 percent chance of an easing this time round on the grounds that it will primarily want to assess the three cuts seen in the second half of 1996.
There is also a feeling that the central bank will want to see the outcome of the union movement's "living wage" claim, which is seen emerging later this month or early March.

And even those analysts who point to last week's benign inflation data as a reason to cut rates again expect the bank will wait until after the release of the quarterly wages report due out on Thursday.

However, despite these reservations on a change in policy, traders will be closely watching the RBA's daily 9.30 a.m. (2230 GMT) dealing intentions this week, a time when it usually announces any alteration in official interest rates.
Tuesday also sees the release of December and fourth quarter retail trade, which may provide fuel for those looking for a reduction in 6.0 percent interest rates this quarter.

The local market underperformed Friday's sharp rally in U.S. Treasuries which followed benign inflation readings in the fourth quarter GDP. The data was seen lessening the chances of the FOMC meeting tightening policy when it meets on Tuesday and Wednesday. The influential U.S. NAPM index is due later today.
